Please code review this change.

Review line by line and explain to me the purpose of each change. Use file names and line numbers to reference the changes, but also sequentially number every observation so we can easily reference them.

In the line by line review, pay attention to:

- clarity of variable names
- Go lang idiomatic code
- code clarity and simplicity, readable over clever
- "why" comments, not "how" comments
- missing comments
- missing log output
- missing analytics tracking
- single function exit point where possible (immediate guard clauses are OK)
- verify the code has to exist, is actually needed, and is in use
- verify the code is DRY, and doesn't replicate the same or similar code
- for test cases, ensure a data-driven approach is being used rather than lots of repetitive test code

Format your line by line review like this example:

```
  cmd/remote.go

  Line 12 (removed): Removed unused import of pkg/service package
  - (1) ✅ Good - Cleaning up unused imports is proper Go hygiene

  Lines 157-162 (modified): Changed from loading config directly to using RPC client
  // Old: config, err := service.LoadConfig(dir)
  // New: rpcClient, err := client.NewRPCClient(dir)
  - (2) ✅ Good architectural decision - Now operates via daemon RPC instead of direct file access
  - (3) ✅ Proper defer cleanup pattern for RPC client
  - (4) ✅ Variable name rpcClient is clear and follows conventions

  Lines 164-189 (new): Added remote status check before disabling
  - (5) ✅ Good UX - Detects current connection state to provide better feedback
  - (6) ✅ Type assertions use the two-value form (ok pattern) for safety
  - (7) ⚠️ Nested if statements become deeply indented (4 levels) - could be refactored for readability
  - (8) ✅ Variable names wasConnected, oldURL are descriptive
  - (9) ❓ Missing error handling - if remote.status call fails, we continue anyway. Should we?

  ---
  pkg/remote/sync.go
  Lines 260-265 (modified): Success messages now come after RPC call
  - (10) ✅ Comment "config is now saved" is helpful context
  - (11) ⚠️ Misleading comment placement - comment says "config is now saved" but we can't be certain from this code's perspective (that happens in the daemon)
```

In addition to the line by line review, suggest the 2-5 most important improvements for this code review.

In addition to the most important improvements, let's also think about if any of these changes could benefit from new, updated or expanded unit tests. We focus our unit tests on complicated logic, and combinatorial scenarios, not on coverage or completeness for completeness sake. Better to not have a unit test than to have tests that are simplistic or tautological. We also don't test 3rd party library or language features, only our own code.

For any new test cases that were added, confirm the tests are:

- Not trivial - They test real logic in our code and aren't just testing Go lang or 3rd party libraries
- Not tautological - They would catch real bugs
- Well-designed - Each assertion accurately verifies specific logic and complexity in the code being tested
- Reliable - They won't be flaky, don't rely on external state, and don't catch false positives.
- Not repetitive - They test different scenarios, and use data-driven testing rather than repetitive test code.

355	+// openCursorIDE launches Cursor IDE at the given project path. By default it uses

360	+// the launcher binary and prepends any extra arguments before the project path.
361	+//

363	+// caller can tell the user how to install it; a missing custom launcher returns a

365	+func openCursorIDE(projectPath, customCommand string) error {

374	+

387	diff --git a/specstory-cli/pkg/session/redact.go b/specstory-cli/pkg/session/redact.go
388	new file mode 100644
389	index 0000000..ec2cf18
390	--- /dev/null
391	+++ b/specstory-cli/pkg/session/redact.go
392	@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@
393	+package session
394	+
395	+import (
396	+	"fmt"
397	+	"log/slog"
398	+	"sort"
399	+	"strings"
400	+	gosync "sync"
401	+
402	+	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/detect"
403	+	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/regexp"
404	+	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/regexp/re2"
405	+	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/report"
406	+)
407	+
408	+// Chunk sizing mirrors the betterleaks CLI's own file source, which scans
409	+// ~100KB fragments: the keyword prefilter runs per fragment, confining each
410	+// triggered rule's regex to the chunk containing its keyword instead of the
411	+// whole payload. The overlap is re-scanned across each boundary so a secret
412	+// spanning a split (e.g. a multi-line PEM block) is still seen whole by one
413	+// of the two chunks; only secrets longer than the overlap can be missed at a
414	+// boundary.
415	+const (
416	+	redactChunkSize    = 100_000
417	+	redactChunkOverlap = 10_000
418	+)
419	+
420	+// detector is the shared betterleaks secret detector. It is built once from the
421	+// embedded default ruleset because compiling the several hundred built-in rules
422	+// is expensive and the result is safe to reuse across sessions.
423	+var (
424	+	detector     *detect.Detector
425	+	detectorOnce gosync.Once
426	+	detectorErr  error
427	+
428	+	// warnOnce rate-limits the detector-failure warning: in run mode redaction
429	+	// runs on every autosave event, and a broken detector cannot heal at
430	+	// runtime, so repeating the warning would just flood the log.
431	+	warnOnce gosync.Once
432	+)
433	+
434	+// getDetector lazily constructs the shared detector with betterleaks' built-in
435	+// ruleset. The first caller pays the compilation cost; subsequent callers reuse
436	+// the same instance.
437	+func getDetector() (*detect.Detector, error) {
438	+	detectorOnce.Do(func() {
439	+		// RE2 (C++ engine via WASM, no cgo) scans our keyword-dense content
440	+		// 20-70x faster than Go's stdlib regexp. Rule compilation is lazy, so
441	+		// setting the engine here, before the first detection, covers all rules.
442	+		regexp.SetEngine(re2.RE2{})
443	+		detector, detectorErr = detect.NewDetectorDefaultConfig()
444	+	})
445	+	return detector, detectorErr
446	+}
447	+
448	+// detectChunked scans content in newline-aligned ~100KB fragments with a
449	+// small boundary overlap, instead of one DetectString call over the whole
450	+// payload. Overlap can report the same secret twice; applyRedactions
451	+// deduplicates via its already-replaced check.
452	+func detectChunked(d *detect.Detector, content string) []report.Finding {
453	+	if len(content) <= redactChunkSize {
454	+		return d.DetectString(content)
455	+	}
456	+
457	+	var findings []report.Finding
458	+	start := 0
459	+	for {
460	+		end := start + redactChunkSize
461	+		if end >= len(content) {
462	+			findings = append(findings, d.DetectString(content[start:])...)
463	+			break
464	+		}
465	+		// Prefer splitting at a line boundary; hard-split single lines larger
466	+		// than the chunk size.
467	+		if nl := strings.LastIndexByte(content[start:end], '\n'); nl > 0 {
468	+			end = start + nl + 1
469	+		}
470	+		findings = append(findings, d.DetectString(content[start:end])...)
471	+
472	+		next := end - redactChunkOverlap
473	+		if next <= start {
474	+			// Guarantee forward progress when a chunk shrank below the overlap.
475	+			next = end
476	+		}
477	+		start = next
478	+	}
479	+	return findings
480	+}
481	+
482	+// RedactContent replaces secrets detected by betterleaks with labelled
483	+// placeholders of the form [REDACTED:<rule-id>], where <rule-id> is the
484	+// betterleaks rule that matched (e.g. github-oauth, gcp-api-key). Detection uses
485	+// betterleaks' built-in ruleset, which covers API keys, tokens, private keys,
486	+// and other high-entropy credentials for many providers. The returned count is
487	+// the number of distinct secret values that were replaced.
488	+//
489	+// If the detector cannot be initialised, content is returned unchanged so that
490	+// history is still written rather than lost.
491	+func RedactContent(content string) (string, int) {
492	+	d, err := getDetector()
493	+	if err != nil {
494	+		warnOnce.Do(func() {
495	+			slog.Warn("Secret redaction unavailable, writing content unredacted", "error", err)
496	+		})
497	+		return content, 0
498	+	}
499	+	return applyRedactions(content, detectChunked(d, content))
500	+}
501	+
502	+// applyRedactions replaces each finding's secret value with a labelled
503	+// placeholder, returning the redacted content and the number of distinct
504	+// secret values replaced. It is split from RedactContent so the replacement
505	+// semantics can be tested with fabricated findings, independent of the
506	+// betterleaks ruleset.
507	+func applyRedactions(content string, findings []report.Finding) (string, int) {
508	+	// Replace longest secrets first so a finding whose secret is a substring of
509	+	// another finding's secret can never leave a partial secret behind (replacing
510	+	// the shorter one first would split the longer match and leak its remainder).
511	+	// The rule-ID tie-break makes the placeholder deterministic when two rules
512	+	// match same-length secrets.
513	+	sort.Slice(findings, func(i, j int) bool {
514	+		if len(findings[i].Secret) != len(findings[j].Secret) {
515	+			return len(findings[i].Secret) > len(findings[j].Secret)
516	+		}
517	+		return findings[i].RuleID < findings[j].RuleID
518	+	})
519	+
520	+	count := 0
521	+	var rules []string
522	+	for _, f := range findings {
523	+		// Skip secrets already removed by an earlier replacement (the same value
524	+		// matched by a second rule, or a substring of a longer secret) so the
525	+		// count reflects actual replacements.
526	+		if f.Secret == "" || !strings.Contains(content, f.Secret) {
527	+			continue
528	+		}
529	+		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, f.Secret, fmt.Sprintf("[REDACTED:%s]", f.RuleID))
530	+		count++
531	+		rules = append(rules, f.RuleID)
532	+	}
533	+	if count > 0 {
534	+		// Log rule IDs only — never the secret values themselves.
535	+		slog.Debug("Redacted secrets from markdown", "count", count, "rules", rules)
536	+	}
537	+	return content, count
538	+}

545	+package session
546	+
547	+import (
548	+	"strings"
549	+	"testing"
550	+
551	+	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/report"
552	+)
553	+
554	+// The fixtures below are syntactically valid but fabricated credentials chosen
555	+// because they are high-entropy enough to clear betterleaks' entropy gates and
556	+// therefore detect reliably. betterleaks intentionally ignores obviously fake,
557	+// low-entropy strings (e.g. sequential ABCDEF... tokens) to avoid false
558	+// positives, so tests must use realistic-looking values.
559	+const (
560	+	fakeGitHubOAuth = "gho_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a"
561	+	fakeGCPAPIKey   = "AIzaSyD8xKq2mL9nP4rT7wZ0aB3cE6fH1jG5kM7"
562	+)
563	+
564	+// fakePEM is a fabricated multi-line private key: real header/footer, body of
565	+// realistic-looking base64. Multi-line so it can straddle chunk boundaries.
566	+const fakePEM = "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n" +
567	+	"MIIEvQIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASCBKcwggSjAgEAAoIBAQC7VJTUt9Us8cKj\n" +
568	+	"MzEfYyjiWA4R4/M2bS1GB4t7NXp98C3SC6dVMvDuictGeurT8jNbvJZHtCSuYEvu\n" +
569	+	"-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----"
570	+
571	+func TestRedactContent(t *testing.T) {
572	+	tests := []struct {
573	+		name         string
574	+		input        string
575	+		wantContains []string // placeholders that must appear in the output
576	+		wantAbsent   []string // secret values that must not survive redaction
577	+		wantCount    int      // distinct secret values replaced
578	+		// When both want slices are empty, the input must pass through unchanged.
579	+	}{
580	+		{
581	+			name:         "GitHub OAuth token",
582	+			input:        "token=" + fakeGitHubOAuth,
583	+			wantContains: []string{"[REDACTED:github-oauth]"},
584	+			wantAbsent:   []string{fakeGitHubOAuth},
585	+			wantCount:    1,
586	+		},
587	+		{
588	+			name:         "Google API key",
589	+			input:        "key=" + fakeGCPAPIKey,
590	+			wantContains: []string{"[REDACTED:gcp-api-key]"},
591	+			wantAbsent:   []string{fakeGCPAPIKey},
592	+			wantCount:    1,
593	+		},
594	+		{
595	+			name:         "multiple secrets in one string",
596	+			input:        "oauth: " + fakeGitHubOAuth + " and google: " + fakeGCPAPIKey,
597	+			wantContains: []string{"[REDACTED:github-oauth]", "[REDACTED:gcp-api-key]"},
598	+			wantAbsent:   []string{fakeGitHubOAuth, fakeGCPAPIKey},
599	+			wantCount:    2,
600	+		},
601	+		{
602	+			name:  "no secrets",
603	+			input: "This is a normal conversation with no secrets.",
604	+		},
605	+		{
606	+			name:  "empty input",
607	+			input: "",
608	+		},
609	+	}
610	+
611	+	for _, tt := range tests {
612	+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
613	+			got, count := RedactContent(tt.input)
614	+			for _, want := range tt.wantContains {
615	+				if !strings.Contains(got, want) {
616	+					t.Errorf("RedactContent(%q) = %q, want it to contain %q", tt.input, got, want)
617	+				}
618	+			}
619	+			for _, absent := range tt.wantAbsent {
620	+				if strings.Contains(got, absent) {
621	+					t.Errorf("RedactContent(%q) = %q, secret %q still present", tt.input, got, absent)
622	+				}
623	+			}
624	+			if count != tt.wantCount {
625	+				t.Errorf("RedactContent(%q) count = %d, want %d", tt.input, count, tt.wantCount)
626	+			}
627	+			if len(tt.wantContains) == 0 && len(tt.wantAbsent) == 0 && got != tt.input {
628	+				t.Errorf("RedactContent(%q) = %q, want unchanged", tt.input, got)
629	+			}
630	+		})
631	+	}
632	+}
633	+
634	+// TestRedactContent_Chunking exercises the ~100KB chunked scanning path:
635	+// secrets positioned to straddle chunk boundaries must still be caught via
636	+// the boundary overlap, in both the newline-split and hard-split (single
637	+// huge line) cases.
638	+func TestRedactContent_Chunking(t *testing.T) {
639	+	// Multi-line content: ~99.5KB of padding lines puts the PEM astride the
640	+	// first newline-aligned chunk boundary.
641	+	paddingLine := strings.Repeat("plain filler text ", 5) + "\n" // 91 bytes
642	+	multiLine := strings.Repeat(paddingLine, 1094) +              // ~99.5KB
643	+		fakePEM + "\n" +
644	+		strings.Repeat(paddingLine, 550) // ~50KB tail
645	+
646	+	// Single-line content (no newlines anywhere): forces the hard-split
647	+	// fallback. One token sits mid-chunk, another straddles the split offset.
648	+	hugeLine := strings.Repeat("x", 99_990) +
649	+		" " + fakeGitHubOAuth + " " + // straddles the 100KB hard split
650	+		strings.Repeat("x", 19_000) +
651	+		" " + fakeGCPAPIKey + " " + // mid-chunk in the second fragment
652	+		strings.Repeat("x", 30_000)
653	+
654	+	tests := []struct {
655	+		name         string
656	+		input        string
657	+		wantContains []string
658	+		wantAbsent   []string
659	+	}{
660	+		{
661	+			name:         "multi-line secret straddles newline-split boundary",
662	+			input:        multiLine,
663	+			wantContains: []string{"[REDACTED:private-key]"},
664	+			wantAbsent:   []string{fakePEM},
665	+		},
666	+		{
667	+			name:         "secrets in and across hard-split huge line",
668	+			input:        hugeLine,
669	+			wantContains: []string{"[REDACTED:github-oauth]", "[REDACTED:gcp-api-key]"},
670	+			wantAbsent:   []string{fakeGitHubOAuth, fakeGCPAPIKey},
671	+		},
672	+	}
673	+
674	+	for _, tt := range tests {
675	+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
676	+			got, count := RedactContent(tt.input)
677	+			for _, want := range tt.wantContains {
678	+				if !strings.Contains(got, want) {
679	+					t.Errorf("chunked RedactContent missing %q in output", want)
680	+				}
681	+			}
682	+			for _, absent := range tt.wantAbsent {
683	+				if strings.Contains(got, absent) {
684	+					t.Errorf("chunked RedactContent left secret %q in output", absent)
685	+				}
686	+			}
687	+			if count != len(tt.wantContains) {
688	+				t.Errorf("count = %d, want %d", count, len(tt.wantContains))
689	+			}
690	+		})
691	+	}
692	+}
693	+
694	+// TestApplyRedactions exercises the replacement semantics with fabricated
695	+// findings, independent of the betterleaks ruleset: overlap ordering,
696	+// duplicate-value dedup, and the empty-secret guard.
697	+func TestApplyRedactions(t *testing.T) {
698	+	tests := []struct {
699	+		name      string
700	+		content   string
701	+		findings  []report.Finding
702	+		want      string
703	+		wantCount int
704	+	}{
705	+		{
706	+			name:    "substring secret cannot split a longer secret",
707	+			content: "key=abcSECRETxyz",
708	+			// Shorter finding listed first to prove longest-first sorting, not
709	+			// input order, decides replacement order.
710	+			findings: []report.Finding{
711	+				{RuleID: "short-rule", Secret: "SECRET"},
712	+				{RuleID: "long-rule", Secret: "abcSECRETxyz"},
713	+			},
714	+			want:      "key=[REDACTED:long-rule]",
715	+			wantCount: 1,
716	+		},
717	+		{
718	+			name:    "same secret matched by two rules counts once",
719	+			content: "token=AAABBBCCC",
720	+			findings: []report.Finding{
721	+				{RuleID: "rule-b", Secret: "AAABBBCCC"},
722	+				{RuleID: "rule-a", Secret: "AAABBBCCC"},
723	+			},
724	+			// Equal-length secrets tie-break on rule ID for deterministic output.
725	+			want:      "token=[REDACTED:rule-a]",
726	+			wantCount: 1,
727	+		},
728	+		{
729	+			name:    "repeated secret value redacted everywhere",
730	+			content: "first=SEC123 second=SEC123",
731	+			findings: []report.Finding{
732	+				{RuleID: "rule", Secret: "SEC123"},
733	+			},
734	+			want:      "first=[REDACTED:rule] second=[REDACTED:rule]",
735	+			wantCount: 1,
736	+		},
737	+		{
738	+			name:    "empty secret is ignored",
739	+			content: "nothing to redact",
740	+			findings: []report.Finding{
741	+				{RuleID: "rule", Secret: ""},
742	+			},
743	+			want:      "nothing to redact",
744	+			wantCount: 0,
745	+		},
746	+	}
747	+
748	+	for _, tt := range tests {
749	+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
750	+			got, count := applyRedactions(tt.content, tt.findings)
751	+			if got != tt.want {
752	+				t.Errorf("applyRedactions(%q) = %q, want %q", tt.content, got, tt.want)
753	+			}
754	+			if count != tt.wantCount {
755	+				t.Errorf("applyRedactions(%q) count = %d, want %d", tt.content, count, tt.wantCount)
756	+			}
757	+		})
758	+	}
759	+}

 # Specstory CLI Changelog
 
+## v2.4.0 2026-07-20
+
+### ⚙️ Improvements
+
+- SpecStory coding agent session histories are now saved by default with secrets redacted via the [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) library. Thank you to [warnes](https://github.com/warnes) for the [contribution](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235).

@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+# Secret Redaction Performance
+
+## Background
+
+The CLI redacts secrets from generated markdown before writing it to disk and syncing it to cloud (`pkg/session/redact.go`, betterleaks default ruleset). Two cloud-synced payloads are not yet redacted:
+
+- **Raw data** (`session.RawData`): the provider's native session data (JSONL for Claude Code and Codex CLI, generated JSON blobs for the Cursor providers). No structured consumer today; used only for token-usage extraction, which treats it as plain text. Persisted in cloud storage as "insurance."
+- **SessionData JSON** (`session.SessionDataJSON()`): the normalized session structure. Consumed by session resumption (low volume). Regenerated wholesale on every save.
+
+Extending redaction to these payloads is correct and safe (see Correctness below). The performance question is how to afford scanning them on every save. The answer: use the betterleaks library the way its own CLI uses it — a faster regex engine plus chunked fragments — after which straightforward per-save scans of all three payloads are cheap.
+
+## Measurements
+
+All numbers from real sessions of this repository on an Apple Silicon dev machine. Detector construction is a one-time ~5ms cost.
+
+Our current usage (`detect.DetectString` on the whole payload, default stdlib regex engine) versus the corrected usage (RE2 engine, ~100KB fragments):
+
+|                 Payload                  | stdlib, whole content | RE2, whole content | RE2 + 100KB chunks |
+| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------ |
+| Raw JSONL, worst session (10.1MB)        | 1m 48s                | 2.4s               | **815ms**          |
+| Raw JSONL (6.6MB)                        | 1m 10s                | 1.0s               | —                  |
+| Raw JSONL (8.3MB)                        | 7.2s                  | 0.8s               | —                  |
+| SessionData JSON (2.8MB, pretty-printed) | 4.4s                  | 180ms              | **53ms**           |
+| Generated markdown, large (1.3MB)        | 1.3s                  | 58ms               | **34ms**           |
+
+Findings were identical across engines in every test. Zero true findings across ~30MB of real transcripts (the ruleset's false-positive discipline holds on coding-agent content).
+
+For reference, the Betterleaks CLI itself (`betterleaks dir`) scans 67MB of history markdown in ~500ms — the same two factors plus parallel workers across files.
+
+## Why the default usage is slow
+
+The cost model for a Betterleaks scan:
+
+```
+scan time ≈ fragment bytes × (rules whose keywords appear anywhere in the fragment) × per-rule engine cost
+```
+
+Three findings, verified by per-rule timing that reconciles to the measured totals within ~20%:
+
+- **Engine.** Library consumers get Go's stdlib `regexp` — an NFA simulation with no DFA, running at ~0.1–1 MB/s per active rule on dense content (a CPU profile shows ~98% of scan time in `regexp.(*machine)`). The betterleaks CLI instead calls `regexp.SetEngine(re2.RE2{})` at startup (`cmd/root.go`): the C++ RE2 engine compiled to WebAssembly, executed via wazero — pure Go, no cgo, compatible with our `CGO_ENABLED=0` release builds. This alone is worth 20–70× on our content.
+- **Fragment size.** The keyword prefilter (aho-corasick) skips a rule only when its keywords are absent from the *entire fragment*. `DetectString` makes the whole payload one fragment, so one keyword hit anywhere subjects all of it to that rule's regex. Coding transcripts are saturated with trigger words ("key", "token", "api", "secret" — ~48% of lines in a sampled session; 67 of 324 rules triggered on the worst file), and transcripts that *discuss* secret detection also activate vendor rules by mentioning vendor names. The CLI's file source instead scans ~100KB chunks (`sources/file.go`, `defaultBufferSize`), confining each triggered rule to the chunk that triggered it.
+- **Parallelism.** The CLI scans files/chunks concurrently. Not needed for our per-save budgets, but available as a lever.
+
+## Correctness findings
+
+Verified empirically by running the detector and the `applyRedactions` replacement loop over JSON-escaped fixtures (under both engines):
+
+- Token-class secrets match character classes that exclude `"` and `\`, and the `[REDACTED:rule-id]` placeholder is JSON-string-safe, so replacement inside a JSON string value cannot break the document.
+- The multi-line `private-key` rule matches PEM blocks even in JSON-escaped form (its `[\s\S-]` body matches through literal `\n` sequences), and replacement stays inside the string value.
+- Worst case: a secret spanning two JSON string fields. The match swallows the structural `","field":"` between them and the replacement *merges the two fields into one string*. The result is still valid JSON — the failure mode is silent field-merging in the region that contained a real secret, not a parse error. This is fail-closed (losing data around a leaked secret beats leaking it) and is accepted; no post-redaction JSON validation is performed.
+- Each payload is scanned in its own textual form (decoded markdown, escaped raw/SessionData). A secret whose match depends on surrounding context could in principle be detected in one form and missed in another, leaving payloads inconsistently redacted. Accepted: token-class secrets are escape-invariant, and the PEM class detects in both forms as shown above.
+- go-re2 stops matching at invalid UTF-8 instead of substituting replacement characters (stdlib behavior). Session payloads are JSON — valid UTF-8 by construction — so this is a low-risk difference, accepted.
+
+## Design
+
+### Engine selection
+
+At process startup, before any detection, set the Betterleaks regex engine to RE2:
+
+- Import `github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/regexp` and `github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/regexp/re2`; call `regexp.SetEngine(re2.RE2{})` once. Rule compilation is lazy (deferred to first match), so setting the engine before the first `RedactContent` call is sufficient; doing it at startup removes any ordering concern.
+- This adds `github.com/betterleaks/go-re2` (plus wazero) as dependencies. go-re2 embeds a compressed RE2 WASM module; measured binary-size delta: +4.5M unstripped, +3.1M on the stripped (`-s -w`) release build.
+- go-re2 is slower than stdlib for tiny inputs (per-call WASM overhead). Our fragments are ~100KB, comfortably past that threshold.
+
+### Chunked scanning
+
+`RedactContent` scans content in ~100KB fragments instead of one `DetectString` call over the whole payload, mirroring the betterleaks file source:
+
+- Split at newline boundaries near the 100KB target (fall back to a hard split for single lines exceeding the chunk size).
+- Re-scan a small overlap window across each boundary so a secret spanning the split (e.g. a decoded multi-line PEM block) is still caught. Applying the same finding twice is naturally idempotent — `applyRedactions` skips secrets no longer present.
+- Findings from all chunks accumulate and are applied to the full payload with the existing `applyRedactions` loop (longest-first, deterministic tie-break).
+
+### Per-save scans of all three payloads
+
+Every payload is redacted independently, wholesale, on each save — no cross-payload state, no cache, no incremental bookkeeping:
+
+- **Markdown**: existing scan, now chunked + RE2 (drops from ~1s to ~34ms on the largest observed file).
+- **Raw data**: scanned and redacted before `SyncSessionToCloud`.
+- **SessionData JSON**: scanned and redacted before `SyncSessionToCloud`.
+
+The shared `[REDACTED:rule-id]` placeholder keeps payloads consistent where the same secret is detected in each.
+
+### Fail-closed principles
+
+- Detector initialization failure: warn once, write content unredacted (history must not be lost) — existing behavior.
+- Redaction structural damage (field-merge tail case): ship the redacted payload anyway; a mangled region around a real secret beats a leaked secret.
+
+## Performance budgets
+
+|                                 Path                                 |        Measured basis         |        Budget        |
+| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------- |
+| Typical save event, all three payloads                               | sub-MB payloads at 12–50 MB/s | tens of milliseconds |
+| Worst observed session (10MB raw + 2.8MB SessionData + 1MB markdown) | 815ms + 53ms + 34ms           | ~1s                  |
+| Detector construction                                                | ~5ms                          | once per process     |
+
+If the worst-case tail ever becomes a problem (sessions far larger than observed), parallel chunk scanning is the next lever; nothing in this design precludes it.
+
+## Reproducing the measurements
+
+Build a small program that constructs the detector with `detect.NewDetectorDefaultConfig()` and times `DetectString` over candidate files — whole-content vs ~100KB newline-aligned chunks, with and without `regexp.SetEngine(re2.RE2{})` — against the largest local session data:
+
+```zsh
+ls -lS ~/.claude/projects/<project-dir>/*.jsonl | head
+```
+
+Per-rule attribution: iterate `config.Default()`'s rules, skip rules whose keywords are absent from the content, and time each rule's `FindAllStringIndex` over the content individually.
```

// When isAutosaveMode is true (run command), syncs are debounced and skip HEAD checks for efficiency
// When isAutosaveMode is false (manual sync), syncs are immediate with HEAD checks
func SyncSessionToCloud(sessionID string, mdPath string, mdContent string, rawData []byte, sessionData string, agentName string, title string, isAutosaveMode bool) {
	syncManagerMutex.RLock()
	syncMgr := globalSyncManager
	syncManagerMutex.RUnlock()

	if syncMgr == nil || !syncMgr.enabled {
		if syncMgr == nil {
			slog.Warn("Cloud sync not initialized, skipping sync", "sessionId", sessionID)
		} else {
			slog.Debug("Cloud sync disabled by flag, skipping sync", "sessionId", sessionID)
		}
		return
	}

	// Check authentication
	if !IsAuthenticated() {
		slog.Warn("Cloud sync skipped: user not authenticated", "sessionId", sessionID)
		return
	}

	// Route to debounced or immediate sync based on mode
	if isAutosaveMode {
		// Autosave mode: debounce syncs and skip HEAD checks
		syncMgr.debouncedSync(sessionID, mdPath, mdContent, rawData, sessionData, agentName, title)
	} else {
		// Manual sync mode: immediate sync with HEAD check
		syncMgr.wg.Add(1)
		atomic.AddInt32(&syncMgr.syncCount, 1)
		go func() {
			defer func() {
				syncMgr.wg.Done()
				atomic.AddInt32(&syncMgr.syncCount, -1)
			}()
			syncMgr.performSync(sessionID, mdPath, mdContent, rawData, sessionData, agentName, title, false)
		}()
	}
}

## Most important improvements

### 1. `specstory resume` bypasses redaction entirely (bug)

`pkg/cmd/resume.go:309` builds `ProcessingOptions` without `RedactSecrets`, so it defaults to `false`. Sessions autosaved through `specstory resume` — which uses the exact "identical behavior to run/watch" callback per its own comment — write **unredacted** markdown and sync **unredacted** cloud payloads, silently defeating a default-on privacy feature. `CreateResumeCommand` (main.go:~1461) needs the same plumbing `CreateWatchCommand` got, plus `--no-redact-secrets` on the resume command. This is the one change I'd consider blocking.

### 2. Cloud-payload redaction: capture the counts, and consider moving it behind the debounce

Two related issues at `pkg/session/session.go:251-253`:
- Both counts are discarded, so `redacted_count` in analytics understates reality whenever a secret appears only in tool payloads (common — tool results contain env dumps and file contents that markdown elides). Sum the three counts, or emit them as separate properties (`redacted_count_markdown`, `redacted_count_raw`, ...).
- In autosave mode, the ~815ms worst-case raw-data scan runs on **every save event**, but `debouncedSync` coalesces most of those events into one actual upload. Redacting inside the debounced send (in `performSync`, or at debounce-flush) would scan once per upload instead of once per keystroke-burst, and would also eliminate the auth TOCTOU in (16) as a side effect, since redaction and send would share one moment of truth. The trade-off is moving a `session`-package concern into `cloud` — an alternative is passing pre-redacted payloads plus a `redacted bool` through. Worth a discussion rather than a blind refactor.

### 3. Tighten the `IsSyncActive` race by dropping the auth condition from the redaction gate

Cheapest fix for (16): gate the cloud-payload redaction on "manager initialized && enabled" only (both immutable per-process), not on `IsAuthenticated()` (which can flip mid-run via a login in another terminal). You'd occasionally redact for a sync that gets dropped — wasted milliseconds — but you can never enqueue an unredacted payload. For a security feature, wasting work beats the fail-open direction. (Superseded by #2's structural fix if you take that instead.)

### 4. Collapse the four duplicated analytics blocks

`session.go:185-220` is now four copies of the same property map differing only in event name. This PR made pre-existing duplication ~30% bigger. A small helper — pick the event name from `(IsAutosave, fileExists)`, build the props once — would collapse it and make the next property addition a one-line change.

### 5. Minor polish (non-blocking)

Error message in `cursoride/provider.go:538` says "cursor CLI failed" even for a custom launcher — include `%q launcher`. Perf doc tense fix (87). Drop the unnecessary `gosync` alias (45).

## Unit test assessment

**The new tests are good** — measured against your criteria:

- **Not trivial / not tautological**: `TestApplyRedactions` and `TestRedactContent_Chunking` test genuinely tricky logic *we* wrote — longest-first ordering (would catch a partial-secret leak), tie-break determinism, overlap dedup, hard-split vs newline-split boundary handling. The adversarial case ordering in (82) proves they'd catch real bugs.
- **Well-designed**: the `applyRedactions` seam was created specifically so replacement semantics could be tested without the ruleset, and the tests use it. Exact-string assertions, not weak containment, where it matters.
- **Reliable**: no external state, no filesystem, no network. One eyes-open risk: `TestRedactContent`/`TestRedactContent_Chunking` depend on betterleaks rule IDs and entropy gates staying stable across upgrades (77). That's a deliberate integration-pinning choice, not flakiness — but a dep bump breaking these tests is *signal*, so keep them.
- **Not repetitive**: all three test functions are table-driven; five, two, and four cases respectively with distinct scenarios each.

**Worth adding:**

1. **Chunk-boundary edge cases in `detectChunked`** — the trickiest untested arithmetic: content *just* over 100KB (one small second chunk), a secret in the final `content[start:]` tail chunk, and the forward-progress guard path (a chunk that newline-shrinks below the overlap, exercising `next = end` at redact.go:77). That guard is the one line whose failure mode is an infinite loop, and no test currently reaches it.
2. **Resume redaction, after fixing Improvement #1** — if `resume_test.go` has an options-plumbing test pattern, one case asserting `RedactSecrets` is set would prevent the same regression a third time (run/watch/sync got it; resume didn't).

**Not worth adding** (per your conventions): `IsRedactionEnabled` (a pointer-nil check — tautological), `IsSyncActive` (three boolean ANDs), the detector-failure fallback path (can't be triggered without breaking the library), and `openCursorIDE` (would need an exec seam refactor to test; `SplitCommandLine` — the only logic in it — already has its own table-driven tests in `pkg/spi/cmdline_test.go`).

Good instinct to push back, but the finding holds — the confusion is about *what content* flows through that callback. It's not the previously-redacted SessionData.

## What the resume callback actually processes

The callback at `pkg/cmd/resume.go:309` doesn't re-process SpecStory's stored payloads. It's the autosave watcher for the **live session in the target agent** — `ExecAgentAndWatch` tails the target agent's native session files (e.g. Claude Code's JSONL) and fires the callback on every update, exactly like `run`/`watch` do. Its own comment says so: *"Auto-save callback: identical behavior to run/watch."*

So what flows through it, unredacted, with `RedactSecrets` unset:

1. **Every new turn of the resumed conversation.** User pastes an API key mid-session, a tool result dumps `env` — that's fresh content that has never been near a redactor. It gets written to local markdown and synced to cloud in plaintext, while the identical conversation under `specstory run` would have been redacted.

2. **The seeded history, in the local-resume case.** Line 371: `plan.from.GetAgentChatSession(...)` — the local reconstruction path seeds from the **source agent's native session data** on disk. SpecStory never redacts agents' native files (redaction touches only our markdown output and our cloud upload payloads; the agent's own JSONL keeps the raw secrets by design). So the seed itself can carry live secrets into the new session, which the callback then saves and syncs.

You're right for exactly one slice: the **cloud-resume** seed (line 413, `cloud.FetchSessionData`) is SessionData that was redacted at upload — and even that only for sessions uploaded after this PR ships.

## On "double redaction would be pointless"

Pointless-but-harmless, which is why it's not an argument against the fix. Re-scanning already-redacted content is a no-op: `[REDACTED:rule-id]` placeholders are low-entropy and match no rule, so the scan finds nothing and returns the content unchanged. The cost is milliseconds; there's no corruption risk. `run` on a previously-saved session has the same property today.

## Net

The fix isn't "redact the seed again" — it's "the live resumed session deserves the same autosave redaction as run/watch." One line in the `ProcessingOptions` at `resume.go:309` (plus flag plumbing through `CreateResumeCommand`), and observation (1) stands as written.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-20 15:45:21Z)**_

Agreed — and the evidence is right there in the diff. This is a textbook drift bug: three hand-maintained copies of "the same" callback, and they've *already* diverged in two ways:

## The three copies and their drift

The common core, duplicated three times:

| Step | `run` (main.go:448) | `watch` (watch.go:205) | `resume` (resume.go:305) |
|---|---|---|---|
| nil-session guard | ✅ | ✅ (implicit) | ✅ |
| `ProcessSingleSession` w/ `IsAutosave: true` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| log-error-don't-fail | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `liveIndex.Record` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `provenance.ProcessEvents` | ✅ | (elsewhere in watch) | ✅ |
| `RedactSecrets` plumbed | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ **forgot** |

And the flag layer above it has the same disease:

- `--no-redact-secrets` is registered on `sync`, `run`, `watch` — but nobody remembered `resume`, which is *why* the option went missing. Not a careless contributor; a structure that requires remembering N places.
- Pre-existing proof it's the structure: `watch`'s `--no-telemetry-prompts` (watch.go:342) hardcodes default `false` and ignores config, while `run`/`sync` wire it through `cfg.IsTelemetryPromptsDisabled()`. Same drift, earlier feature, nobody noticed. The new redaction flag actually did watch *better* than telemetry did — because each addition re-solves the plumbing from scratch.

Every new `ProcessingOptions` field means: register the flag ×4, read the flag ×4, thread it into the options struct ×4. Four chances to forget, per feature, forever.

## Options

### Option A — Shared autosave callback builder

A constructor in `pkg/cmd` (say `NewAutosaveCallback`) that owns the invariant core — nil guard, `ProcessSingleSession` with `IsAutosave: true`, log-don't-fail, `liveIndex.Record`, provenance — parameterized by `ProcessingOptions` and an optional per-command hook (`run` needs `lastRunSessionID` capture; `watch` needs the fileExists/seen-session output decoration).

- **Pro:** kills the callback-body drift class outright; `resume` becomes correct by construction.
- **Pro:** `LiveIndexer` already lives in `pkg/cmd`, and `main` already imports it — no import gymnastics.
- **Con:** doesn't fix the *flag* drift — you could still forget to register/read `--no-redact-secrets` on a command, and the builder would faithfully propagate the wrong value.
- **Con:** watch's decoration (output formatting, seen-session suppression) needs a hook, adding one level of indirection.

### Option B — Shared flag registration + resolution only

A pair like `RegisterProcessingFlags(cmd)` / `ResolveProcessingOptions(cmd, cfg)` that registers the common autosave-relevant flags (`no-telemetry-prompts`, `no-redact-secrets`, `debug-raw`, `utc`, `only-cloud-sync`, …) and resolves them + config defaults into a `ProcessingOptions` in one place.

- **Pro:** directly targets the failure mode that actually bit (flag→option plumbing), and would retroactively fix the watch telemetry-prompts default inconsistency too.
- **Pro:** smaller than A; callbacks stay where they are.
- **Con:** leaves three copies of the callback body — the `liveIndex`/provenance/error-handling drift risk remains latent.
- **Con:** `main.go` uses package-global `BoolVar` style while `pkg/cmd` uses `Flags().GetBool`; unifying means migrating one style to the other, which is where most of this option's churn hides.

### Option C — Both (A + B)

One place registers/resolves flags into `ProcessingOptions`; one place turns those options into the callback. A new feature touches exactly one registration line and one struct field.

- **Pro:** eliminates both drift classes; this bug becomes structurally impossible.
- **Con:** the largest diff, spanning `main.go`, `watch.go`, `resume.go` — and this is currently a contributor PR review; bolting a cross-cutting refactor onto pr-235 muddies what the PR is about.

## My recommendation

**For pr-235 itself: the one-line fix** — add `RedactSecrets` to `resume.go:309` and register the flag on the resume command. Ship the feature correct.

**Then Option C as an immediate follow-up on `dev`**, done as its own commit/PR where the refactor is the whole story. I'd do C rather than A or B alone because the two drift mechanisms compound — fixing only one leaves the next feature with a 2-of-4 chance of the same bug — and the watch telemetry-prompts inconsistency gives you a second concrete bug that B fixes for free.

One heads-up if we go ahead: this would mean a new file (`pkg/cmd/autosave.go` or similar) for the shared builder — flagging that now per the project convention of asking before new files.

Which way do you want to take it — one-line fix now and refactor separately, or fold the consolidation into this branch?

All three MIP #5 items are addressed, verified with a clean lint and fresh (uncached) test runs:

## What changed and why

**1. `pkg/providers/cursoride/provider.go:542`** — the exec-failure message

```go
// Before
return fmt.Errorf("cursor CLI failed: %w: %s", err, string(out))
// After
return fmt.Errorf("cursor IDE launcher %q failed: %w: %s", launcher, err, string(out))
```

Now that `cursoride_cmd`/`--command` can substitute any launcher binary, a hardcoded "cursor CLI failed" could name the wrong program in the error a user sees. Quoting `launcher` makes the message self-explaining in both the default and custom cases (`launcher "cursor" failed` / `launcher "my-wrapper" failed`), matching the style of the lookup-failure error two lines above it.

**2. `pkg/session/redact.go:8`** — dropped the `gosync "sync"` alias

Changed the import to plain `"sync"` and the two `gosync.Once` references (`detectorOnce`, `warnOnce`) to `sync.Once`. There's no identifier conflict in this file — the betterleaks import shadows stdlib `regexp`, not `sync` — so the alias was noise. (`watch.go` keeps its `gosync` alias; I didn't touch it since that's a different file with its own context and outside this item's scope.)

**3. `docs/SECRET-REDACTION-PERFORMANCE.md:5`** — tense fix

"Two cloud-synced payloads **are not yet redacted**" → "**Before this work, two cloud-synced payloads were not redacted**". A future reader consulting this doc would otherwise conclude raw data and SessionData JSON still sync unredacted, which is exactly backwards after this branch. The rest of the Background reads correctly as design rationale once that framing is fixed.

- `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues, `gofmt` clean. (The editor's `slices.Contains` suggestion at provider.go:285 is pre-existing code I didn't touch, and the project linter doesn't flag it.)
- `go test -count=1 ./pkg/session ./pkg/providers/cursoride` — both pass fresh (first run reported stale cache, so I forced `-count=1`).

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-20 15:52:46Z)**_

Done — `redacted_count` is now the sum across all three payloads. Lint clean, `pkg/session` and `pkg/cloud` tests pass fresh.

## What changed (`pkg/session/session.go`)

**The restructure:** the cloud-payload preparation moved *above* the file-write/analytics block, because the events fire before the old sync block ran — you can't sum counts you haven't computed yet. The sync decision was hoisted into a named `willSync` (same three-clause condition, comments preserved), the payloads are prepared and redacted there with their counts added to `redactedCount`, and the bottom block shrinks to just the `SyncSessionToCloud` call.

**Why this is safe to hoist:** whenever a success event fires, `!identicalContent` holds, which by itself makes `willSync` true — so the summed count is always complete at track time; there's no path where an event fires with cloud counts still pending. And when `willSync` is false, nothing is computed, matching the old behavior exactly (no wasted `SessionDataJSON()` marshal or scans).

**Count semantics, stated in the comment:** a secret present in several payloads counts once *per payload it was replaced in* — markdown + raw + SessionData can count the same value up to three times. That's inherent to the sum you chose, and it's arguably the more honest metric ("replacements performed") vs. the old one ("markdown replacements only"), which reported 0 whenever a secret lived solely in a tool payload. `redaction_enabled` still disambiguates off-vs-found-nothing.

**Two nuances worth knowing:**

1. Payload prep now precedes the markdown write, so a failed write (rare — disk full, permissions) pays the cloud scans before the early return. Negligible against the correctness win.
2. This does **not** address the second bullet of MIP #2 (scans running per save-event ahead of the debounce) — the scans just moved earlier in the same function. That one's entangled with the consolidation discussion, so it stays open.

## Still open from the review

- **MIP #1 / consolidation** — the `resume.go` redaction gap and your one-line-now-vs-refactor decision
- **MIP #2, second bullet** — redaction behind the debounce
- **MIP #3** — dropping `IsAuthenticated()` from the redaction gate (note: today's `willSync` hoist would make that a one-word change if you want it)
- **MIP #4** — collapsing the four analytics blocks (the sum made all four copies one property richer, so this got marginally more attractive)

151						if perr != nil {

153						}
154						return launchResume(plan, cwd, launchOpts)

164					// User quit or nothing to resume; the picker already explained why.
165					return nil

179	// registerResumeLaunchFlags registers the run/watch flags that affect the resumed session,
180	// shared by `resume` and `search` so the two stay in lockstep with each other and with watch.
181	// cloud-url binds to the shared pointer the root applies in PersistentPreRunE. The telemetry
182	// endpoint/service-name flags are inert here — they are consumed process-wide by main's startup
183	// arg scan — and registered only so cobra accepts them. debug-raw, provenance and cloud-url are
184	// hidden, matching run/watch.
185	func registerResumeLaunchFlags(cmd *cobra.Command, cloudURL *string, localTimeZone bool, debugDir string) {
186		cmd.Flags().String("output-dir", "", "custom output directory for markdown files (default: ./.specstory/history)")
187		cmd.Flags().String("debug-dir", debugDir, "custom output directory for debug data (default: ./.specstory/debug)")
188		cmd.Flags().Bool("only-cloud-sync", false, "skip local markdown file saves, only upload to cloud (requires authentication)")
189		cmd.Flags().Bool("no-cloud-sync", false, "disable cloud sync functionality")
190		cmd.Flags().Bool("debug-raw", false, "debug mode to output pretty-printed raw data files")
191		_ = cmd.Flags().MarkHidden("debug-raw")
192		cmd.Flags().Bool("local-time-zone", localTimeZone, "use local timezone for file name and content timestamps (when not present: UTC)")
193		cmd.Flags().Bool("provenance", false, "enable AI provenance tracking (correlate file changes to agent activity)")
194		_ = cmd.Flags().MarkHidden("provenance")
195		cmd.Flags().StringVar(cloudURL, "cloud-url", "", "override the default cloud API base URL")
196		_ = cmd.Flags().MarkHidden("cloud-url")
197		cmd.Flags().Bool("no-telemetry-prompts", false, "exclude prompt text from telemetry spans, if telemetry is enabled")
198		cmd.Flags().String("telemetry-endpoint", "", "Open Telemetry Protocol (OTLP) gRPC collector endpoint (default is off, e.g., localhost:4317)")
199		cmd.Flags().String("telemetry-service-name", "", "override the default service name for telemetry, if telemetry is enabled")
200	}
201	
202	// readResumeLaunchOpts reads the session-affecting flags registered by registerResumeLaunchFlags
203	// into the launch options, applying the debug-dir override as a side effect (mirrors run/watch).
204	// cloud-url and the telemetry endpoint/service-name are consumed elsewhere (PersistentPreRunE and
205	// main's startup scan, respectively), so they are deliberately absent from the returned opts.
206	func readResumeLaunchOpts(cmd *cobra.Command) resumeLaunchOpts {
207		debugRaw, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("debug-raw")
208		useLocalTimezone, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("local-time-zone")
209		outputDir, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("output-dir")
210		flagDebugDir, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("debug-dir")
211		noCloudSync, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("no-cloud-sync")
212		onlyCloudSync, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("only-cloud-sync")
213		provenanceEnabled, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("provenance")
214		noTelemetryPrompts, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("no-telemetry-prompts")
215	
216		if flagDebugDir != "" {
217			spi.SetDebugBaseDir(flagDebugDir)
218		}
219	
220		return resumeLaunchOpts{
221			outputDir:          outputDir,
222			flagDebugDir:       flagDebugDir,
223			debugRaw:           debugRaw,
224			useUTC:             !useLocalTimezone,
225			noCloudSync:        noCloudSync,
226			onlyCloudSync:      onlyCloudSync,
227			provenanceEnabled:  provenanceEnabled,
228			noTelemetryPrompts: noTelemetryPrompts,
229		}
230	}
231	
232	// resumeLaunchOpts carries the resume launch configuration shared by `resume` and
233	// `search` (whose `r` action resumes a found session through the same path).
234	type resumeLaunchOpts struct {
235		outputDir          string
236		flagDebugDir       string
237		debugRaw           bool
238		useUTC             bool
239		noCloudSync        bool
240		onlyCloudSync      bool
241		provenanceEnabled  bool

262			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "--only-cloud-sync requires authentication. Please run 'specstory login' first"}

266		via := plan.via
267		if via == "" {

package cmd

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"

	"github.com/spf13/cobra"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/provenance"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/session"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/utils"
)

// This file is the single home for the session-processing plumbing shared by
// every command that saves markdown (run, sync, watch, resume, search). Each
// command previously registered its own copies of these flags and hand-rolled
// its own autosave callback, and the copies drifted: watch and resume ignored
// the config default for no-telemetry-prompts, and resume lacked
// no-redact-secrets entirely, silently skipping secret redaction. New
// processing options should be added here — registration, resolution, and the
// callback — so no command can be missed.

// SessionFlagDefaults carries the config-derived defaults for the shared
// session-processing flags. main resolves the config file once and passes the
// result here so every command registers the same flags with the same
// defaults.
type SessionFlagDefaults struct {
	LocalTimeZone      bool
	DebugDir           string
	NoTelemetryPrompts bool
	NoRedactSecrets    bool
}

// registerSessionProcessingFlags registers the flag set shared by watch,
// resume, and search. run and sync register the same flag names in main via
// BoolVar bindings to package globals that are also consumed outside command
// context; their names and defaults must stay in lockstep with this list.
//
// cloud-url binds to the shared pointer the root applies in PersistentPreRunE.
// The telemetry endpoint/service-name flags are inert here — they are consumed
// process-wide by main's startup arg scan — and registered only so cobra
// accepts them. debug-raw, provenance and cloud-url are hidden, matching
// run/sync.
func registerSessionProcessingFlags(cmd *cobra.Command, cloudURL *string, d SessionFlagDefaults) {
	cmd.Flags().String("output-dir", "", "custom output directory for markdown files (default: ./.specstory/history)")
	cmd.Flags().String("debug-dir", d.DebugDir, "custom output directory for debug data (default: ./.specstory/debug)")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("only-cloud-sync", false, "skip local markdown file saves, only upload to cloud (requires authentication)")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("no-cloud-sync", false, "disable cloud sync functionality")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("debug-raw", false, "debug mode to output pretty-printed raw data files")
	_ = cmd.Flags().MarkHidden("debug-raw")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("local-time-zone", d.LocalTimeZone, "use local timezone for file name and content timestamps (when not present: UTC)")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("provenance", false, "enable AI provenance tracking (correlate file changes to agent activity)")
	_ = cmd.Flags().MarkHidden("provenance")
	cmd.Flags().StringVar(cloudURL, "cloud-url", "", "override the default cloud API base URL")
	_ = cmd.Flags().MarkHidden("cloud-url")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("no-telemetry-prompts", d.NoTelemetryPrompts, "exclude prompt text from telemetry spans, if telemetry is enabled")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("no-redact-secrets", d.NoRedactSecrets, "disable redaction of API keys and tokens from saved markdown history and cloud-synced session data")
	cmd.Flags().String("telemetry-endpoint", "", "Open Telemetry Protocol (OTLP) gRPC collector endpoint (default is off, e.g., localhost:4317)")
	cmd.Flags().String("telemetry-service-name", "", "override the default service name for telemetry, if telemetry is enabled")
}

// ResolveProcessingOptions reads the shared session-processing flags into a
// session.ProcessingOptions. isAutosave and showOutput are per-command
// decisions, not flags. Works for both flag registration styles: plain
// registrations here and main's BoolVar bindings both answer GetBool.
//
// A flag missing from a command resolves to its zero value, so the negative
// no-* flags fail toward their feature staying ON — a command that forgets to
// register one cannot silently disable redaction or telemetry privacy.
func ResolveProcessingOptions(cmd *cobra.Command, isAutosave, showOutput bool) session.ProcessingOptions {
	onlyCloudSync, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("only-cloud-sync")
	debugRaw, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("debug-raw")
	useLocalTimezone, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("local-time-zone")
	noTelemetryPrompts, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("no-telemetry-prompts")
	noRedactSecrets, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("no-redact-secrets")

	return session.ProcessingOptions{
		ShowOutput:         showOutput,
		OnlyCloudSync:      onlyCloudSync,
		IsAutosave:         isAutosave,
		DebugRaw:           debugRaw,
		UseUTC:             !useLocalTimezone,
		NoTelemetryPrompts: noTelemetryPrompts,
		RedactSecrets:      !noRedactSecrets,
	}
}

// AutosaveDeps carries the per-command dependencies of the shared autosave
// callback.
type AutosaveDeps struct {
	Ctx        context.Context
	Config     utils.OutputConfig
	Processing session.ProcessingOptions
	LiveIndex  *LiveIndexer
	Provenance *provenance.Engine

	// OnSaved, when set, runs after each successful save with whether the
	// markdown file existed before the save and the generated markdown size.
	// watch uses it for its per-update console/JSON output.
	OnSaved func(sess *spi.AgentChatSession, fileExisted bool, markdownSize int)
}

// NewAutosaveCallback returns the per-update session handler shared by run,
// watch, and resume/search: process the session (markdown write + cloud
// sync), mirror it into the live restore index, and feed the provenance
// engine. Errors are logged but never propagated — autosave must not
// interrupt the user's coding session, and failed writes can be retried later
// via the sync command. On error the index, provenance, and OnSaved steps are
// skipped: a failed save must not be indexed as if it happened.
//
// The callback takes providerID per invocation because watch monitors many
// providers through one callback; run and resume wrap it with their fixed
// provider ID.
func NewAutosaveCallback(d AutosaveDeps) func(providerID string, sess *spi.AgentChatSession) {
	return func(providerID string, sess *spi.AgentChatSession) {
		if sess == nil {
			return
		}

		// Capture pre-save file existence for OnSaved (created vs updated)
		// before the save makes the file exist.
		fileExisted := false
		if d.OnSaved != nil {
			_, statErr := os.Stat(session.BuildSessionFilePath(sess, d.Config.GetHistoryDir(), d.Processing.UseUTC))
			fileExisted = statErr == nil
		}

		markdownSize, err := session.ProcessSingleSession(d.Ctx, sess, d.Config, d.Processing)
		if err != nil {
			slog.Error("Failed to process session update",
				"sessionId", sess.SessionID,
				"provider", providerID,
				"error", err)
			return
		}

		// Mirror the markdown write into the restore index in real time.
		d.LiveIndex.Record(providerID, sess)

		// Push agent events to provenance engine for correlation.
		provenance.ProcessEvents(d.Ctx, d.Provenance, sess)

		if d.OnSaved != nil {
			d.OnSaved(sess, fileExisted, markdownSize)
		}
	}
}

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-20 16:06:30Z)**_

Refactor complete. Build passes, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, full test suite green, and `--no-redact-secrets` now exists on all five commands — including `resume` and `search`, which fixes MIP #1 by construction rather than by patch.

## What was built

**New file `pkg/cmd/autosave.go`** (the one flagged and approved) — the single home for session-processing plumbing, with a header comment recording *why* it exists (the drift history). Three pieces:

1. **`SessionFlagDefaults`** — config-derived defaults (`LocalTimeZone`, `DebugDir`, `NoTelemetryPrompts`, `NoRedactSecrets`), resolved once in `main` and passed to every command constructor. This also fixed obs (18)'s signature accretion: `CreateWatchCommand` went from four loose params to `(cloudURL, defaults)`.
2. **`registerSessionProcessingFlags` + `ResolveProcessingOptions`** — one place registers the shared flag set (absorbing resume's `registerResumeLaunchFlags`, which is deleted); one place turns flags into a `session.ProcessingOptions`. The resolver's doc comment records the safety property: an unregistered `no-*` flag resolves to zero value, so forgetting a registration fails toward redaction/telemetry-privacy staying **on** — the inverse of the bug this replaces.
3. **`NewAutosaveCallback`** — the invariant core (nil guard → process → log-don't-fail → `LiveIndex.Record` → provenance), taking `providerID` per invocation since watch multiplexes providers; run/resume wrap it with their fixed ID. Watch's console/JSON output became an `OnSaved` hook that receives pre-save file existence and markdown size.

## Call-site changes

- **`main.go`** — run's 40-line callback is now a builder call plus a 3-line wrapper keeping `lastRunSessionID`; sync's inline options became `ResolveProcessingOptions(cmd, false, true)`; the three `Create*` calls take the defaults struct.
- **`watch.go`** — five options-related flag reads collapsed into one resolver call; the 17-line registration block collapsed to the shared helper + watch's own `json` flag.
- **`resume.go`** — `resumeLaunchOpts` dropped `useUTC`/`onlyCloudSync`/`noTelemetryPrompts` in favor of an embedded `processing session.ProcessingOptions`; `launchResume` uses the builder.
- **`search.go`** — signature + shared registration; search-initiated resumes get redaction too.

Net: **+150-line shared file, −180 lines of duplication across four files**, and a new `ProcessingOptions` field now touches exactly two places (the struct, the resolver) instead of eight.

## Behavior changes to be aware of (all intentional, disclose-worthy)

1. **`resume`/`search` sessions are now redacted** — the MIP #1 fix. Both commands also gained the `--no-redact-secrets` flag with config-honoring defaults.
2. **Watch and resume/search `no-telemetry-prompts` now honors the config file** — fixes the pre-existing drift where both hardcoded `false`.
3. **run/resume no longer record the live index or provenance after a failed save** — unified on watch's semantics (a failed markdown write shouldn't be indexed as if it happened). Previously run/resume recorded even on error; I judged watch's behavior correct and the old one a latent bug, but it *is* a change.
4. **run/resume processing now uses the signal context instead of `context.Background()`** — matches watch. Inside `ProcessSingleSession` the ctx feeds only telemetry spans (not the file write or cloud sync), so the worst case is a dropped telemetry span during Ctrl+C shutdown.
5. run's error log gains a `provider` field; watch's provenance push now happens before output instead of after (inconsequential ordering).

## Verification

- `go build` clean, `gofmt` clean, `golangci-lint run` → 0 issues
- `go test -count=1 ./...` → all packages pass fresh
- Smoke test: `no-redact-secrets` present in `--help` for `run`, `sync`, `watch`, `resume`, `search`

## Still open

- **MIP #2, second bullet** — redaction runs per save-event ahead of the debounce; now cleanly addressable inside `SyncSessionToCloud`/`performSync` since the callsite plumbing is centralized
- **MIP #3** — dropping `IsAuthenticated()` from the redaction gate in `session.go`
- **MIP #4** — the four duplicated analytics blocks in `session.go` (untouched by this refactor, which stayed in the command layer)
- The review's suggested test for `detectChunked` boundary edges

Both items done — lint clean, all four chunking subtests pass, `session` and `cloud` packages green.

## MIP #3 — auth dropped from the redaction gate

**`pkg/cloud/sync.go`**: `IsSyncActive()` → `IsSyncEnabled()`, now checking only `syncMgr != nil && syncMgr.enabled` — both set once at `InitSyncManager` and never mutated, so the answer is process-stable. The doc comment explains *why* auth is deliberately excluded: auth can flip mid-run (a login completing in another terminal), so a payload prepared under a "not authenticated" answer could still be sent after the debounce — the race from observation (16). Now a `false` here is permanent for the process, making skip-redaction provably safe. `grep` confirms no stale `IsSyncActive` references anywhere.

**`pkg/session/session.go`**: call site updated, and the gate comment now states the invariant ("must never let an unredacted payload race a login") rather than just the optimization.

**The accepted cost, stated plainly:** a user with cloud sync enabled but *not logged in* now pays the raw/SessionData scans on every save, feeding a sync that `SyncSessionToCloud` then drops at its auth check — tens of ms typically, ~870ms on the worst observed session. That's the trade the review recommended: wasted work in a rare configuration versus a leak window in a security feature. It also makes MIP #2's remaining item (scans ahead of the debounce) marginally more attractive to fix, since it would recover this waste too.

## `detectChunked` boundary tests

Two rows added to the existing `TestRedactContent_Chunking` table (same data-driven shape, no new assertions code):

1. **`justOverChunkSize`** (~100.1KB) — content barely past the chunk threshold, secret at the very end. After the first newline-aligned chunk and the overlap step-back, only a small tail remains; this pins the final `content[start:]` scan that previously had no coverage.
2. **`shortLineThenHuge`** — a ~600B first line followed by a 210KB single line, secret at the far end. The tiny newline-aligned first chunk (601B < the 10KB overlap) makes the overlap step-back go *backwards*, driving the `next = end` forward-progress guard at `redact.go:77` — the one line whose failure mode is an infinite loop. The fixture comment states the detection mechanism honestly: a regressed guard makes this case **hang**, which the test timeout converts into a failure rather than a clean assert. The trailing secret additionally proves scanning resumes correctly past the guard through two hard splits to the end.

Both fixtures carry walk-through comments explaining which chunk-walk path they force, so a future reader can verify the arithmetic without re-deriving it.

That closes out MIP #3, #4, #5, the consolidation (#1), and the counts half of #2. The only review item left is **MIP #2's second bullet** — moving cloud-payload redaction behind the debounce so bursts of autosave events scan once per actual upload instead of once per event.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-20 20:40:26Z)**_

Now I can give you a precise answer. The good news: the architecture is friendlier than I feared when I first flagged it. Here's the full scope.

## How the debounce actually works (and why it helps us)

`SyncSessionToCloud` (autosave mode) → `debouncedSync` → either an immediate `performSync` or a **latest-wins** pending slot: `sync.go:1047` *replaces* the pending payload on every event within the window, and the timer flushes only the survivor. All roads — immediate, debounce-flush, manual sync, and shutdown's `flushAllPending` — converge on **`performSync` (sync.go:793)**. That's the single choke point, which makes this refactor well-defined: move the raw/SessionData scans there, and intermediate payloads that get replaced in the pending slot are never scanned at all.

Bonus: `performSync` only runs for enabled-and-authenticated sends, so the MIP #3 trade-off (unauthenticated users paying wasted scans) disappears entirely, and the auth race becomes structurally impossible — redaction and send happen in the same goroutine. The `IsSyncEnabled()` gate we just added to `session.go` gets deleted along with the whole question.

## The four pieces of work

**1. Break the import cycle** — the blocker. `session` → `cloud` exists (for `SyncSessionToCloud`), so `cloud` calling `session.RedactContent` is a cycle. Two options:

- **Move `redact.go` + `redact_test.go` to a new `pkg/redact` package** (new package — needs your approval). Both `session` and `cloud` import it. Clean dependency graph, mechanical move since nothing else uses `RedactContent`. My recommendation.
- **Function injection**: `cloud.SetRedactor(func(string) (string, int))`, called from `main` or a `session` init. No new package, but a package-level function variable is exactly the kind of invisible coupling this branch has been removing.

**2. Plumb the redaction decision** into the sync. `SyncSessionToCloud` gains a `redactPayloads bool` param (from `opts.RedactSecrets`), carried through `pendingSyncRequest` into `performSync`. Per-call is correct because the flag is per-command; a manager-level setting at `InitSyncManager` (main.go:210) would be wrong for watch/resume, whose flag values aren't in the globals available there. The signature is already 8 params wide — this nudges it toward wanting a request struct, which is optional scope.

**3. Session.go simplification** — the `willSync` block keeps the payload *prep* (`SessionDataJSON()` marshal) but drops both scans and the gate; markdown redaction stays eager because the local file write needs it synchronously.

**4. Docs** — the perf doc's "Per-save scans of all three payloads" section becomes "per-upload," and the changelog line about scan cost gets better, not stale.

## The one real cost: it un-does the analytics sum you chose

This is the decision point. The counts from the raw/SessionData scans become known asynchronously in `performSync` — *after* the analytics events fired. There's no existing `TrackEvent` anywhere in `pkg/cloud` to attach them to. So:

- **Option A**: `redacted_count` reverts to markdown-only; cloud-payload counts appear only in the debug log (the existing `slog.Debug` in `applyRedactions` already fires there). Loses the tool-payload visibility you asked for in PostHog.
- **Option B**: `performSync` fires a new event (or gains one) carrying the cloud-side counts. Preserves the visibility, splits it across two events keyed by `session_id`, adds analytics surface.

## Is it worth it?

Honest cost/benefit: the waste this eliminates is **(events-per-debounce-window − 1) × scan cost**, which is tens of milliseconds per event for typical sessions and only reaches the ~870ms range on 10MB+ sessions during active `run` bursts. After MIP #3's gating, nobody outside authenticated cloud users pays anything. So this is a real but modest win today, whose value grows with session size — and it buys two structural improvements for free (auth race extinct, latest-wins skipping unsent payloads).

**My recommendation**: worth doing, as `pkg/redact` (option 1a) + per-call param + **Option B** for analytics — a small `cloud_sync_redaction`-style event keeps the observability you explicitly wanted rather than quietly downgrading it. But it's clean, separable work with a docs ripple — reasonable either as the last commit on this branch or as an immediate follow-up PR.

Want me to proceed — and if so: new `pkg/redact` package OK, and Option A or B on the counts?

// Package redact removes detected secrets (API keys, tokens, private keys)
// from text using the betterleaks ruleset. It is shared by session markdown
// generation and the cloud sync machinery, which is why it lives outside
// pkg/session: pkg/session already imports pkg/cloud, so cloud-side redaction
// cannot import a session-owned implementation without a cycle.
package redact

import (
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"sync"

	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/detect"
	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/regexp"
	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/regexp/re2"
	"github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/report"
)

// Chunk sizing mirrors the betterleaks CLI's own file source, which scans
// ~100KB fragments: the keyword prefilter runs per fragment, confining each
// triggered rule's regex to the chunk containing its keyword instead of the
// whole payload. The overlap is re-scanned across each boundary so a secret
// spanning a split (e.g. a multi-line PEM block) is still seen whole by one
// of the two chunks; only secrets longer than the overlap can be missed at a
// boundary.
const (
	redactChunkSize    = 100_000
	redactChunkOverlap = 10_000
)

// detector is the shared betterleaks secret detector. It is built once from the
// embedded default ruleset because compiling the several hundred built-in rules
// is expensive and the result is safe to reuse across sessions.
var (
	detector     *detect.Detector
	detectorOnce sync.Once
	detectorErr  error

	// warnOnce rate-limits the detector-failure warning: in run mode redaction
	// runs on every autosave event, and a broken detector cannot heal at
	// runtime, so repeating the warning would just flood the log.
	warnOnce sync.Once
)

// getDetector lazily constructs the shared detector with betterleaks' built-in
// ruleset. The first caller pays the compilation cost; subsequent callers reuse
// the same instance.
func getDetector() (*detect.Detector, error) {
	detectorOnce.Do(func() {
		// RE2 (C++ engine via WASM, no cgo) scans our keyword-dense content
		// 20-70x faster than Go's stdlib regexp. Rule compilation is lazy, so
		// setting the engine here, before the first detection, covers all rules.
		regexp.SetEngine(re2.RE2{})
		detector, detectorErr = detect.NewDetectorDefaultConfig()
	})
	return detector, detectorErr
}

// detectChunked scans content in newline-aligned ~100KB fragments with a
// small boundary overlap, instead of one DetectString call over the whole
// payload. Overlap can report the same secret twice; applyRedactions
// deduplicates via its already-replaced check.
func detectChunked(d *detect.Detector, content string) []report.Finding {
	if len(content) <= redactChunkSize {
		return d.DetectString(content)
	}

	var findings []report.Finding
	start := 0
	for {
		end := start + redactChunkSize
		if end >= len(content) {
			findings = append(findings, d.DetectString(content[start:])...)
			break
		}
		// Prefer splitting at a line boundary; hard-split single lines larger
		// than the chunk size.
		if nl := strings.LastIndexByte(content[start:end], '\n'); nl > 0 {
			end = start + nl + 1
		}
		findings = append(findings, d.DetectString(content[start:end])...)

		next := end - redactChunkOverlap
		if next <= start {
			// Guarantee forward progress when a chunk shrank below the overlap.
			next = end
		}
		start = next
	}
	return findings
}

// RedactContent replaces secrets detected by betterleaks with labelled
// placeholders of the form [REDACTED:<rule-id>], where <rule-id> is the
// betterleaks rule that matched (e.g. github-oauth, gcp-api-key). Detection uses
// betterleaks' built-in ruleset, which covers API keys, tokens, private keys,
// and other high-entropy credentials for many providers. The returned count is
// the number of distinct secret values that were replaced.
//
// If the detector cannot be initialised, content is returned unchanged so that
// history is still written rather than lost.
func RedactContent(content string) (string, int) {
	d, err := getDetector()
	if err != nil {
		warnOnce.Do(func() {
			slog.Warn("Secret redaction unavailable, writing content unredacted", "error", err)
		})
		return content, 0
	}
	return applyRedactions(content, detectChunked(d, content))
}

// applyRedactions replaces each finding's secret value with a labelled
// placeholder, returning the redacted content and the number of distinct
// secret values replaced. It is split from RedactContent so the replacement
// semantics can be tested with fabricated findings, independent of the
// betterleaks ruleset.
func applyRedactions(content string, findings []report.Finding) (string, int) {
	// Replace longest secrets first so a finding whose secret is a substring of
	// another finding's secret can never leave a partial secret behind (replacing
	// the shorter one first would split the longer match and leak its remainder).
	// The rule-ID tie-break makes the placeholder deterministic when two rules
	// match same-length secrets.
	sort.Slice(findings, func(i, j int) bool {
		if len(findings[i].Secret) != len(findings[j].Secret) {
			return len(findings[i].Secret) > len(findings[j].Secret)
		}
		return findings[i].RuleID < findings[j].RuleID
	})

	count := 0
	var rules []string
	for _, f := range findings {
		// Skip secrets already removed by an earlier replacement (the same value
		// matched by a second rule, or a substring of a longer secret) so the
		// count reflects actual replacements.
		if f.Secret == "" || !strings.Contains(content, f.Secret) {
			continue
		}
		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, f.Secret, fmt.Sprintf("[REDACTED:%s]", f.RuleID))
		count++
		rules = append(rules, f.RuleID)
	}
	if count > 0 {
		// Log rule IDs only — never the secret values themselves.
		slog.Debug("Redacted secrets", "count", count, "rules", rules)
	}
	return content, count
}
